summary: Iter 153 — Bot story-caption fix validated end-to-end. New signature `_generate_story_caption(persona, feud)` correctly injects title / party_a / party_b / category into the user_prompt (verified via a fake LlmChat stub that captures the prompt). Post-response refusal filter drops LLM outputs containing any of the markers ('non posso', 'mi servirebbe', 'non ho abbastanza', 'puoi darmi', 'post di riferimento', 'riferimento a un post', 'non riesco') → returns None so the caller stores comment='' instead of the refusal text. `_bot_create_story` integration test: when the LLM refuses, the story is still inserted (kind='feud') with an empty comment; when the LLM returns a valid caption, that exact caption is persisted. `story_prompt_for` system prompt now contains the reinforcement clauses 'NON introdurre la risposta' / 'NON chiedere contesto'. Regression: `_generate_comment` signature unchanged (persona, feud, side); iter146 anti-dup + 1/24h quota still hold; /api/stories/feed reachable; /api/feuds returns 200; /api/auth/signup + /api/auth/anonymous work. DB inspection confirms the one-shot cleanup: 0 bot stories out of 99 currently in DB carry refusal captions. Total: 25/25 PASS (18 iter153 + 7 iter146 regression) in 2.11s.

critical_code_review_comments: bot_engine.py:971-1029 — the fix is layered defensively: (a) inject feud context into the user_prompt so the model has grounding, (b) system prompt reinforces 'no intro / no context-asking' via story_prompt_for, (c) post-response refusal filter as a safety net. Even if the LLM ignores clauses (a)+(b), (c) still kills the bad output. Sound design.

bot_engine.py:890 — caller uses `caption = await _generate_story_caption(...)` then `(caption or '')[:200]`. Combined with the new filter returning None on refusal, this produces a story doc with comment=''. The frontend's StoryViewer must gracefully render empty caption (should already do so — the field was optional in the schema).

bot_engine.py:1017-1023 — refusal_markers list is case-folded via `.lower()` before matching, which is correct. Substring match (not word-boundary) means a caption legitimately using 'non posso credere' would ALSO be filtered as false-positive. This is acceptable given the low-caption-length constraint (60 chars) and the empty-string fallback, but note the tradeoff: recall > precision on this filter.
bot_personas.py:593-608 — story_prompt_for hardcodes the reinforcement clauses (not persona-dependent), which is fine here. Same tone-agnostic instruction for all 100 bots.

rca_of_issue: User reported two failure modes in bot stories: (1) meta refusals stored verbatim as captions ('non posso commentare perche non c\'e un post di riferimento'), (2) captions unrelated to the shared feud. RCA identified by main agent: `_generate_story_caption` was called with `persona` only, and the user_prompt was a bare 'Genera la frase per la story.' The system prompt (`story_prompt_for`) said 'stai condividendo un post che ti ha colpito' but no post was ever specified → model hallucinated random content OR politely refused asking for the post. Fix: (a) new signature (persona, feud) with user_prompt injecting title/party_a/party_b/category, (b) system prompt reinforced with 'NON introdurre la risposta / NON chiedere contesto', (c) post-response refusal filter as safety net returning None so caller stores empty caption. Testing agent validated all three layers via fake-LlmChat mocking + real DB integration + prompt-content assertions. 25/25 tests PASS. Historical DB was cleaned one-shot by main agent (28 refusal captions removed → 0 remaining, confirmed).
